open_points.subject: execute_function bounds validation

Clamp bounds to the release ceilings
Reject the execution as contract_violation
Raise an exception

open_points.subject: execute_function input tuple validation

options: Assume the caller always supplies consistent tuples
Return contract_violation
Raise an exception
Match payloads to ports by payload.port rather than tuple position

open_points.subject: execute_function duplicate port names

Let the last duplicate win
Assume duplicates are impossible

Fit-check inputs using bounds.output_bytes and return contract_violation
Fit-check inputs using another ceiling

open_points.subject: execute_function malformed value input

options: Return contract_violation
Return crashed
Raise from execute_function
Decode valid JSON without verifying canonical form

open_points.text: a value port's canonical JSON decoded to Python, a file port's bytes, and for cardinality many a list of those in order

Multiple JsonPayload entries with the same port name
A payload form not described in the model surface

open_points.subject: execute_function code delivery

Pass code through an inherited descriptor and exec it in a new module
Pass code as a command-line argument

open_points.subject: execute_function exchange-directory contents
open_points.text: one fresh private exchange directory bound read-write and bounded by the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SANDBOX_SCRATCH_BYTES_MAX constant
open_points.question: Which artifacts count against the scratch ceiling: code, inputs, outputs, runner protocol files, and trap/resource records, or only files created by agent code?
options: Everything stored in the exchange directory
Only agent-created files
Only output files
Code and agent-created files but not protocol metadata

open_points.subject: execute_function scratch enforcement
open_points.text: bounded by the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SANDBOX_SCRATCH_BYTES_MAX constant
open_points.question: How must a per-execution directory be hard-limited to this byte count, and how is an over-limit condition distinguished from unrelated filesystem errors?

Use a quota-backed filesystem
Monitor directory size and kill after it exceeds the limit
Rely on free space and classify ENOSPC

open_points.subject: execute_function bubblewrap command
open_points.text: MUST start bubblewrap with new user, PID, IPC, UTS and network namespaces

options: Use the minimal flags directly implied by the note
Add standard hardening flags such as capability drops and a new session
Treat any command satisfying the stated observable isolation as valid

open_points.subject: execute_function runtime-path bindings
open_points.text: exactly the host paths of the imported SANDBOX_RUNTIME_PATHS constant bound read-only

Bind paths under a private runtime prefix
Reject missing or overlapping entries
Let bubblewrap behavior decide

open_points.subject: execute_function interpreter invocation
open_points.text: which hold the release's Python runtime and standard library
open_points.question: How is RELEASE_SANDBOX_INTERPRETER used to identify the executable, given that the constant is also described by probe_sandbox as the expected implementation-and-version output?

Treat it only as an expected version string and derive the executable from a runtime path
Use the current process's Python executable

open_points.subject: RELEASE_SANDBOX_INTERPRETER
open_points.text: RELEASE_SANDBOX_INTERPRETER: str

Implementation/version identity
A string encoding both, with an unspecified format

open_points.subject: execute_function environment
open_points.text: the environment cleared and then set exactly to the imported SANDBOX_ENVIRONMENT constant
open_points.question: Does 'exactly' apply only to the runner process environment, or must bubblewrap itself also be launched with no inherited variables; and may Python inject or require variables such as locale or hash-seed settings?
options: Only the sandboxed runner must receive the exact mapping
Both bubblewrap and the runner must receive exactly the mapping
Additional deterministic Python variables may be added
open_points.default_guess: Give the runner exactly SANDBOX_ENVIRONMENT and launch bubblewrap with a separately sanitized host environment.

open_points.subject: execute_function trap target resolution
open_points.text: replace every entry point named by the imported SANDBOX_TRAPPED_FUNCTIONS constant
open_points.question: What syntax do the strings use, which modules or namespaces are searched, and what happens when a named target is missing or cannot be replaced?
options: Fully qualified dotted names
Names in builtins only
Names in a predefined but unstated registry
Fail the execution when a target cannot be installed
open_points.default_guess: Treat them as fully qualified dotted names and fail as crashed if a mandatory trap cannot be installed.

open_points.subject: execute_function no-argument traps
open_points.text: those of the imported SANDBOX_TRAPPED_WITHOUT_ARGUMENT constant with ones that raise when called without an argument
open_points.question: Do calls with only keyword arguments count as having an argument, and are omitted optional arguments distinguished from an explicit None?
options: Any positional or keyword argument avoids the trap
Only a positional argument avoids the trap
None is treated the same as omission
Use the original callable's signature binding
open_points.default_guess: Any supplied positional or keyword argument avoids this specific trap, including explicit None unless separately prohibited.

open_points.subject: execute_function trapped class methods
open_points.text: every method of the class named by the imported SANDBOX_TRAPPED_CLASS constant
open_points.question: Does 'every method' include inherited methods, descriptors, static/class methods, dunder methods, and methods added after trap installation?
options: Only methods directly present in the class dictionary
All callable attributes including inherited methods
A fixed but unstated method list
Replace the class itself instead
open_points.default_guess: Trap callable attributes directly declared on the named class, including static and class methods.

open_points.subject: execute_function seeded constructor rule
open_points.text: when constructed without a seed or with None, and that class's seed method when called on an instance without a seed or with None
open_points.question: How is the seed argument identified across positional and keyword calls, and what happens with extra arguments or a keyword whose name is not specified?
options: The first positional argument or keyword named seed
Bind against the original signature
Any non-None argument counts as a seed
open_points.default_guess: Bind against the original callable signature and inspect its seed parameter.

open_points.subject: execute_function trap durability
open_points.text: MUST replace every entry point ... with one that raises
open_points.question: Must the runner prevent agent code from restoring, reloading, monkey-patching, or obtaining pre-trap references to the original entry points?
options: Initial replacement is sufficient
Continuously enforce replacements
Block imports/reloads that expose originals
Rely on the audit hook for operations that emit audit events
open_points.default_guess: Install replacements before loading agent code and rely on the audit hook for underlying sensitive operations.

open_points.subject: execute_function audit-hook event policy
open_points.text: install an audit hook that raises on socket, subprocess and ctypes use
open_points.question: Which exact Python audit event names and argument patterns constitute socket, subprocess, ctypes, os.system, posix_spawn, exec-family, thread-start, and process use?
options: Use a fixed exhaustive event-name table
Reject by event-name prefixes
Trap only the specifically named events
Combine audit events with monkey patches
open_points.default_guess: Use an explicit exhaustive event table and supplement operations for which CPython emits no suitable audit event.

open_points.subject: execute_function thread process accounting
open_points.text: The runner's audit hook, on os.fork and on starting a thread, counts the tasks
open_points.question: How can the audit hook observe every thread start if the runtime does not provide a guaranteed general audit event for thread creation, and which APIs must be wrapped to satisfy the requirement?
options: Assume the selected runtime emits a thread-start audit event
Patch threading and low-level thread entry points
Poll /proc instead of intercepting starts
The requirement cannot be implemented portably as written
open_points.default_guess: Patch both threading and low-level thread creation APIs in addition to using audit events.

open_points.subject: execute_function process-count scan
open_points.text: counts the tasks of the environment's proc
open_points.question: At what instant and by what /proc traversal are processes and threads counted, how are races handled, and does the pending new task count before it exists?
options: Count current /proc tasks and add one before creation
Count after creation and terminate excess tasks
Maintain a runner-side counter
Combine a counter with /proc reconciliation
open_points.default_guess: Count current /proc tasks immediately before creation and add one for the pending task.

open_points.subject: execute_function caught process-limit errors
open_points.text: writes a resource hit to the channel and raises, so the execution concludes resource_exhausted even when the code catches the error
open_points.question: If the channel reports both a process resource hit and a trap hit, or the execution later times out, which record is authoritative?
options: Apply the global stated outcome order
Use the first channel record
Always prefer the process resource hit
open_points.default_guess: Apply the stated global outcome order, so timeout wins, then resource_exhausted.

open_points.subject: execute_function RLIMIT process allowance
open_points.text: set above bounds.process_count by the tasks the runner and bubblewrap need
open_points.question: What exact additive allowance is used, and how is it derived across bubblewrap versions and launch topologies?
options: A fixed constant allowance
Measure the wrapper tasks at runtime
Set a generously larger release-defined value
Use process_count directly despite wrapper tasks
open_points.default_guess: Measure the known wrapper/runner baseline and set the limit to that baseline plus bounds.process_count.

open_points.subject: execute_function memory limit
open_points.text: address space limited to bounds.memory_bytes with setrlimit
open_points.question: Which setrlimit resource is used, which processes receive it, whether limits are per-process or aggregate across descendants, and how wrapper/runtime overhead is treated are not specified.
options: RLIMIT_AS on the runner and inherited descendants
RLIMIT_DATA
An aggregate cgroup limit in addition to setrlimit
RLIMIT_AS including all runner overhead
open_points.default_guess: Use RLIMIT_AS on the runner before loading code, inherited by descendants, accepting that it is per-process and includes runtime overhead.

open_points.subject: execute_function memory exhaustion detection
open_points.text: A memory ... bound counts as hit only when the parent observes it from outside: the environment was killed for it, or a MemoryError ... escaped run
open_points.question: How does the parent distinguish a memory-limit kill or allocation failure from an unrelated signal, abnormal exit, or runner failure?
options: Classify specific signals as memory exhaustion
Require an explicit runner resource record
Inspect external memory measurements
Treat ambiguous abnormal exits as crashed
open_points.default_guess: Require either an escaped MemoryError record or external evidence that measured memory reached the limit; otherwise classify as crashed.

open_points.subject: execute_function peak memory usage
open_points.text: resources_used with elapsed wall_time_ms, peak memory_bytes
open_points.question: How is peak memory_bytes measured, over which processes, whether wrapper processes count, and what value is returned when measurement is unavailable?
options: Maximum RSS summed across runner descendants
Maximum per-process RSS
Kernel resource-usage maximum including wrappers
Return zero if unavailable
open_points.default_guess: Measure the peak aggregate RSS of sandboxed code and runner tasks, excluding bubblewrap wrapper processes, and use zero only if no sample is possible.

open_points.subject: execute_function deadline origin
open_points.text: the monotonic_ns reading taken when the environment starts plus bounds.wall_time_ms in nanoseconds
open_points.question: What event is 'when the environment starts': before spawning bubblewrap, after bubblewrap starts, after runner initialization, or immediately before loading agent code?
options: Immediately before spawning bubblewrap
When the runner signals readiness
Immediately before module loading
After the run call begins
open_points.default_guess: Take the reading immediately before spawning bubblewrap.

open_points.subject: execute_function deadline enforcement
open_points.text: once a later monotonic_ns reading reaches it — it kills every process of the environment
open_points.question: How are completion at the deadline, polling granularity, timer setup, kill signals, grace periods, and races between a normal result and deadline detection resolved?

Accept a completed result received before the deadline observation
Use a timer process/thread with immediate SIGKILL
Send TERM then KILL
open_points.default_guess: Deadline wins if the parent has not received and validated completion before a reading reaches it; then use immediate SIGKILL.

open_points.subject: execute_function elapsed wall time
open_points.text: resources_used with elapsed wall_time_ms
open_points.question: Are nanoseconds converted by flooring, ceiling, or rounding, and is elapsed time measured through cleanup or only through execution completion?
options: Floor execution duration
Ceil execution duration
Round to nearest millisecond
Include cleanup time
open_points.default_guess: Floor monotonic elapsed time through execution termination, excluding subsequent cleanup.

open_points.subject: execute_function kill and reap scope

Use a process group
Enumerate /proc repeatedly
Use a cgroup

open_points.subject: execute_function cleanup confirmation
open_points.text: after every process of the environment is reaped and the exchange directory is removed; when either cannot be confirmed

Verify no matching processes and path absence

Retry cleanup until the wall deadline
open_points.default_guess: Require successful process wait/no remaining descendants and confirmed path absence; treat ENOENT as removed and make no execution retry.

open_points.subject: execute_function cleanup outcome precedence

Apply cleanup_failed only after an otherwise succeeded execution
Preserve the earlier outcome but set detail_code cleanup_failed
The listed outcome order takes precedence

A file in the exchange directory
A Unix socket inaccessible to agent code
A separate trusted monitor process

Files in the exchange directory
Inherited non-standard file descriptors
Embed some values in generated runner source

Allow all access to the mounted /proc and minimal /dev
Reject agent access but perform trusted operations before installing the hook

Use default json.dumps then canonical_bytes

Sum of canonical byte lengths of list elements

Materialize fully, then count and reject
Let the runner enforce a transport limit

open_points.subject: execute_function resource usage output_bytes

open_points.question: What output_bytes value is reported for malformed, unserializable, trapped, crashed, timed-out, partially received, or over-limit output?

Zero unless a full return value was received
The attempted total even when above the bound
Clamp to bounds.output_bytes

open_points.subject: execute_function outcome classification

open_points.question: How are runner setup/protocol errors, malformed channel messages, serialization failures inside the runner, signals, and bubblewrap launch failures divided between crashed and contract_violation?
options: Trusted setup/protocol/launch failures are crashed; returned-value encoding failures are contract_violation
All channel failures are crashed
All errors caused by returned data are contract_violation

open_points.subject: execute_function failure_detail exception rendering

A structured JSON object rendered as text
Message only
Qualified module.TypeName plus message

open_points.subject: execute_function failure_detail truncation

Reserve bytes for an ellipsis
Replace invalid surrogates before truncation
Fail rendering and return no detail

Suppress it for sandbox_violation
Include details only for crashed outcomes

Suppress it for resource outcomes
Include only MemoryError, not OSError

The cleanup exception text
A fixed cleanup-failed message

open_points.subject: probe_sandbox bubblewrap lookup
open_points.text: when the bubblewrap executable, bwrap, cannot be found on the process's PATH

options: Use shutil.which('bwrap') against the host environment
Search SANDBOX_ENVIRONMENT PATH
Invoke 'bwrap' and rely on exec lookup
Require an absolute configured path

open_points.subject: execute_function bubblewrap availability

Return crashed
Run the full probe implicitly
Assume probe_sandbox was called

open_points.subject: probe_sandbox version parsing
open_points.text: bwrap --version, which prints "bubblewrap" and the version, names a version other than the imported RELEASE_BWRAP_VERSION constant

options: Require stdout exactly 'bubblewrap ' plus the constant after trimming one final newline
Extract the first version token
Search either stream for the expected version
